rationale: Tests comprehension of the determinants that shape a health plan, which is the core content of block 4. Students must distinguish which factors genuinely influence health planning in the Indian context.

Tests understanding of the health planning cycle's phases. The six-phase cycle culminating in monitoring and evaluation is central content of block 7. Students must distinguish sequential from concurrent operation.

Applies health economics tool selection to a realistic scenario. Block 7 covers CEA, CBA, and CUA in detail. Students must identify which tool is appropriate when outcomes are measured in natural health units.
Tests understanding of the PDSA cycle's fundamental principle from block 8. Students must know that PDSA favours small-scale iterative testing rather than large-scale direct implementation.
Tests recall of a key NHP 2017 target — the GDP allocation goal — which is central factual content from block 6. This is a high-yield exam fact from Park.

Applies health economics concepts from block 9 — distinguishing types of health expenditure. Students must correctly classify out-of-pocket expenditure in the context of India's catastrophic health financing burden.
